chapter_title_en: Patman's Falling in Love with Avtandil
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Captivated by the disguised Avtandil's beauty during a banquet, Patman Khatun falls passionately in love with him (illustrating the lower, earthly passion contrasted with Tinatin's and Nestan's chivalric 'mijnuroba' in the Prologue).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
სჯობს სიშორე დიაცისა, ვისგან ვითა დაითმობის:
გილიზღებს და შეგიკვეთებს, მიგინდობს და მოგენდობის,
მართ ანაზდად გიღალატებს, გაჰკვეთეს, რაცა დაესობის,
და მით დიაცსა სამალავი არასთანა არ ეთხრობის.
stanzas.english_translation: Better, for him who can bear it, is aloofness from woman; she plays with thee and pleases thee, she wins thee over and trusts thee; but in a trice she betrays thee, she cuts whatever pierces; so a secret should never be told to a woman.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 44 ('Patman's Falling in Love with Avtandil', Stanza 1081; Wardrop Stanza 1059): Part of the narrative sequence in which captivated by the disguised Avtandil's beauty during a banquet, Patman Khatun falls passionately in love with him (illustrating the lower, earthly passion contrasted with Tinatin's and Nestan's chivalric 'mijnuroba' in the Prologue).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ფატმან ხათუნს ავთანდილის გულსა ნდომა შეუვიდა,
სიყვარული მეტის-მეტი მოემატა, ცეცხლებრ სწვიდა.
დამალვასა ეცდებოდა, მაგრა ჭირთა ვერ მალვიდა,
და იტყვის: “რა ვქმნა, რა მერგების!” აწვიმებდა, ცრემლთა ღვრიდა.
stanzas.english_translation: Desire of Avt’handil went into the heart of Dame P’hatman, love grew from more to more, it burned her like fire, she essayed to conceal it, but could not hide her woes, she said: "What am I to do, what will avail me?" She rained, she poured forth tears.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 44 ('Patman's Falling in Love with Avtandil', Stanza 1082; Wardrop Stanza 1060): Part of the narrative sequence in which captivated by the disguised Avtandil's beauty during a banquet, Patman Khatun falls passionately in love with him (illustrating the lower, earthly passion contrasted with Tinatin's and Nestan's chivalric 'mijnuroba' in the Prologue).

stanzas.english_translation: "If I tell him this, alas! he will be wroth, even the sight of him will become rare to me; if I tell him not, I cannot endure it, the fire will become more intense. I will speak, let me die or live, let one (or other) be my lot! How can the physician cure him who tells not what hurts him?"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 44 ('Patman's Falling in Love with Avtandil', Stanza 1083; Wardrop Stanza 1061): Part of the narrative sequence in which captivated by the disguised Avtandil's beauty during a banquet, Patman Khatun falls passionately in love with him (illustrating the lower, earthly passion contrasted with Tinatin's and Nestan's chivalric 'mijnuroba' in the Prologue).

key_maxim_en: Grant me wings that I may fly, reach my desire! (Stanza 1304)
